v.why: Replacing a cut edge 0 with a 3x3 conv restores the main path from the input, which gains far more than swapping one non-none op for another.
Adding a conv to an empty direct input-to-output edge gains more than replacing an op already on that edge.
Edge 5 feeds the output, so giving it a conv when it is empty adds a lot of capacity compared with replacing an existing op.
Filling a removed edge with a conv gains more than a swap from skip or pool.
Going from no edge to a learned conv is a larger gain than changing between existing ops.
Activating the empty intermediate edge with a conv gains more than a swap from another op.
Removing a 3x3 conv from the input edge costs far more than removing a skip or pool, or an edge that is already none.
Deleting a conv on the direct input-to-output edge hurts more than deleting a weaker op.
Adding a skip to an empty direct edge improves gradient flow and gains more than replacing a conv with a skip, which loses accuracy.
Removing a conv on an edge into the output node drops accuracy more than removing a weak op.

Most of them follow one pattern: an edit that fills an empty edge (current op is `none`) with a useful op should gain more than the same edit replacing an existing op. The reverse also holds, so removing a conv edge costs more than removing a weaker edge.
